title: Praxis Special Education: Early Childhood/Early Intervention (5692) - 200 Source Questions + 300 Guided Review
description: Contains 200 original source questions, 0 assistant-authored independent practice questions, and 300 source-derived guided-review activities. The assistant audit found 134 distinct independent content kernels. Two 100-item diagnostics, an exact-blueprint 120-item timed simulation, targeted feedback, and a native learning library for birth-through-age-eight early intervention and early childhood special education practice.
contentReview: Assistant audit completed: 200 independent-practice items contain 134 distinct content kernels and 66 parallel variants under the normalized test. 300 additional activities are guided reasoning transformations, not independent exam questions. The 500-distinct-question target is not met.
disclaimer: Independent preparation material, not affiliated with or endorsed by ETS. Results are not official forms, scaled scores, pass predictions, licenses, screenings, diagnoses, eligibility or placement decisions, legal advice, or substitutes for current federal, state, local, tribal, or program requirements.

domains.label: Legal and Ethical Practices and Professionalism

items.prompt: A kindergarten early childhood special educator notices that one child reaches several language milestones later than same-age peers. What is the most appropriate first interpretation?
choices: Broad developmental patterns allow wide variation, so the team should gather multi-source evidence across settings before drawing conclusions.
Falling below the typical classroom average on language milestones establishes a developmental disability that warrants formal eligibility.
The team should assign a provisional disability label promptly so specialized speech-language interventions can begin before gathering family input.
Chronological age norms become uninformative once a child trails same-age peers, so expectations should be based on informal adult impressions instead.
items.rationale: Milestones provide useful reference points, not stand-alone diagnoses. Educators should document functioning across domains, contexts, and time and involve qualified team members before attributing a pattern to disability. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Correct. Milestones provide useful reference points, not stand-alone diagnoses. Educators should document functioning across domains, contexts, and time and involve qualified team members before attributing a pattern to disability. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Classroom averages reflect one peer group rather than a diagnostic standard, and early language variation can stem from experience, exposure, or home-language patterns rather than a disability.
Assigning a provisional disability label before multidisciplinary evaluation and family input bypasses IDEA safeguards and risks misidentifying typical developmental variation as an impairment.
Chronological age remains an essential benchmark for interpreting developmental expectations and selecting age-respectful instructional routines, even when a young child needs targeted supports.

items.prompt: A young child solves multistep problems during small-group instruction but rarely begins the same work during a noisy whole-class period. What should the early childhood special educator examine first?
choices: Conclude that the young child has not yet retained the underlying academic skill and re-teach the lesson from the beginning.
Compare task demands, environmental conditions, supports, and performance across both settings.
Lower the academic complexity of the independent assignment so the young child can finish without using classroom supports.
Treat the drop in task initiation during the busier period as willful avoidance and add a stricter compliance consequence.
items.rationale: Performance reflects an interaction among young child skills, task demands, supports, and context. Comparing conditions can identify a removable barrier before the team changes expectations or infers a stable trait. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Because the young child already demonstrates the skill in the structured setting, the gap points to contextual or support barriers rather than a loss of conceptual understanding.

Correct. Performance reflects an interaction among young child skills, task demands, supports, and context. Comparing conditions can identify a removable barrier before the team changes expectations or infers a stable trait. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Reducing academic complexity lowers expectations unnecessarily when the young child has already shown the ability to meet the target under supportive environmental conditions.
Interpreting context-dependent disengagement as intentional defiance overlooks sensory, organizational, or initiation barriers that can be addressed proactively through environmental supports.

items.prompt: An early childhood special educator wants to understand a young child’s self-regulation needs. Which information is most useful?
choices: A single global behavior rating scale completed by a previous early childhood special educator at the start of the school year.
The young child’s primary disability eligibility category paired with a general list of typical classroom accommodations.
Current observations of triggers, strategies used, recovery patterns, and successful routines.
Whole-class averages showing how long most same-age peers sustain independent work without requesting early childhood special educator support.
items.rationale: Self-regulation is best understood through specific, current observations of what precedes difficulty, how the young child responds, which strategies help, and whether patterns differ by setting or task. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: An outdated global rating summarizes broad impressions from another context and fails to identify the specific triggers, warning signs, and calming strategies relevant to current routines.
Eligibility labels describe broad qualifying criteria rather than individual regulation profiles, so relying on category lists misses the young child’s actual antecedents and effective coping tools.

Correct. Self-regulation is best understood through specific, current observations of what precedes difficulty, how the young child responds, which strategies help, and whether patterns differ by setting or task. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Peer-group averages show general classroom norms but do not reveal what overwhelms this individual young child or which environmental adjustments help restore engagement.

items.prompt: A multilingual young child has difficulty following rapid oral directions in English but demonstrates the task after a peer models it. Which interpretation is best?
choices: Difficulty demonstrating understanding through rapid English oral tasks provides sufficient evidence to suspect an intellectual disability.
Peer modeling and visual representations should be removed during checks so the early childhood special educator can measure the young child’s true academic mastery.
Information about how the young child performs in the home language is outside school accountability and should be set aside during planning.
Language access may affect how knowledge is shown, so gather culturally and linguistically appropriate evidence.
items.rationale: Difference is not disability. The team should distinguish language acquisition and access from disability by using multiple methods, appropriate language supports, and information about performance in the young child’s languages. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Limited proficiency in rapid English instructions reflects second-language processing demands, not impaired intellectual functioning; accurate demonstration via modeling or visuals argues against cognitive deficit.
Stripping away modeling or visual supports confounds English language load with content mastery, making assessment data less valid rather than more accurate.
Home-language performance is crucial evidence for distinguishing language acquisition from disability and helps educators build on concepts the young child already understands.

Correct. Difference is not disability. The team should distinguish language acquisition and access from disability by using multiple methods, appropriate language supports, and information about performance in the young child’s languages. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.

items.prompt: A young child with a disability is embarrassed when an adult uses babyish materials for a functional routine. What principle should guide revision?
choices: Use age-respectful materials while adapting task steps and supports to current young child needs.
Select instructional materials strictly by developmental age estimate so the formatting matches early-childhood readiness charts.
Postpone functional and daily-living instruction until the young child achieves independent mastery on grade-level academic standards.
Assign helpful same-age peers to perform the functional routine for the young child so embarrassing instructional materials are unnecessary.
items.rationale: Instruction can be individualized without sacrificing dignity. Materials and contexts should be chronological-age respectful, while prompts, task steps, and response modes are adapted to the young child’s present performance. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Correct. Instruction can be individualized without sacrificing dignity. Materials and contexts should be chronological-age respectful, while prompts, task steps, and response modes are adapted to the young child’s present performance. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Matching materials to early-childhood aesthetics undermines dignity, peer belonging, and motivation when adult or adolescent formats can target the same prerequisite skills effectively.
Delaying essential daily-living instruction until full grade-level mastery denies functional independence and violates the balance between academic access and life-skills preparation.
Having peers complete the routine removes authentic learning opportunities, fosters dependence, and prevents the young child from building self-determined functional skills.

items.prompt: A young child performs a social routine only with one familiar adult. Which plan best promotes generalization?
choices: Continue drilling the skill in the original instructional setting until accuracy stays high across several additional months.
Teach across planned variations in people, materials, and natural settings, then fade prompts.
Introduce multiple unrelated social and communication targets simultaneously so the young child practices broader flexibility right away.
End direct instruction once mastery appears in the familiar setting and monitor whether transfer emerges spontaneously over time.
items.rationale: Generalization is more likely when instruction deliberately varies relevant people, materials, and settings, reinforces the skill in natural routines, and gradually transfers stimulus control away from adult prompts. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Over-practicing in one controlled setting with one adult strengthens narrow stimulus control and rarely transfers without deliberate instruction across natural partners and environments.

Correct. Generalization is more likely when instruction deliberately varies relevant people, materials, and settings, reinforces the skill in natural routines, and gradually transfers stimulus control away from adult prompts. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Adding unrelated targets at the same time increases cognitive load and interferes with consolidating the specific cue-response link the young child needs to transfer.
Hoping for spontaneous transfer—often called train-and-hope—frequently fails for young children who need explicit programming across settings, natural cues, and reinforcement contingencies.

items.prompt: A team is writing a young child profile. Which statement is most useful for planning?
choices: The young child performs at a low-functioning developmental level across most structured and unstructured school routines.
Because the young child has an autism diagnosis, the young child prefers fixed classroom schedules and dislikes unexpected changes.
The young child completes a two-step visual routine independently and needs one verbal cue when steps change.
The young child operates at a developmental stage several years below same-age same-age peers in daily classroom independence.
items.rationale: Objective descriptions identify a demonstrated strength, a specific condition, and the support needed. Global labels and assumptions based on category do not tell the team what to teach or how to measure change. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Broad deficit labels such as low-functioning are non-specific, lack measurable baseline data, and fail to show what the young child can already do or which prompts help.
Inferring preferences from a diagnostic label stereotypes the young child instead of documenting observable classroom performance, specific conditions, and effective supports.

Correct. Objective descriptions identify a demonstrated strength, a specific condition, and the support needed. Global labels and assumptions based on category do not tell the team what to teach or how to measure change. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Age-equivalent estimates oversimplify uneven skill profiles and do not specify the observable behaviors or instructional cues the team needs to write measurable goals.

items.prompt: A young child’s participation drops after a recent family move and change in transportation. How should the school respond?
choices: Attribute the sudden drop in classroom participation to progression of the young child’s underlying disability profile.
Recommend moving the young child to a more restrictive special education classroom so academic expectations can be reduced.
Keep classroom planning focused on curriculum pacing because housing and transportation factors fall outside school instruction.
Weigh environmental disruptions alongside disability needs and coordinate supports respectfully.
items.rationale: Development and learning are influenced by environmental as well as biological factors. A responsive team gathers context, protects privacy, stabilizes access, and avoids treating a situational change as proof of a new disability need. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Blaming an acute performance drop on an existing disability overlooks clear situational stressors such as disrupted sleep, attendance, or routines that require stabilization supports.
Changing placement to a more restrictive setting violates LRE principles when the decline coincides with temporary external disruptions rather than an inability to learn with supports.
Ignoring major environmental stressors misses actionable school-based resources—such as flexible check-ins, McKinney-Vento coordination, and counseling—that directly affect access to learning.

Correct. Development and learning are influenced by environmental as well as biological factors. A responsive team gathers context, protects privacy, stabilizes access, and avoids treating a situational change as proof of a new disability need. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.

items.prompt: An early childhood special educator records one difficult morning and says a young child has lost a previously learned skill. What evidence is needed before changing the program?
choices: Gather repeated observations and work samples under representative conditions and compare them with baseline data.
Revise the instructional program right away because the most recent classroom observation reflects the young child’s current true level.
Review the young child’s disability classification report to confirm whether regression is commonly associated with that label.
Postpone gathering additional evidence until the scheduled annual IEP meeting so classroom routines remain uninterrupted.
items.rationale: A single observation may be affected by health, context, fatigue, or task features. Repeated measures and comparison with baseline information support a more reliable decision about whether performance truly changed. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Correct. A single observation may be affected by health, context, fatigue, or task features. Repeated measures and comparison with baseline information support a more reliable decision about whether performance truly changed. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
A single low session is vulnerable to fatigue, illness, distraction, or testing glitches and provides insufficient reliability to justify major programmatic changes.
General category expectations cannot verify whether an individual young child experienced genuine skill regression; direct longitudinal performance data are required.
Waiting until an annual review without collecting follow-up probes leaves the team unable to tell whether the dip was temporary or signals an urgent instructional need.

items.prompt: A young child with a specific learning disability reads grade-level text accurately but cannot organize written paragraphs. Which response is best?
choices: Deliver uniform remedial instruction across all core academic subjects so the young child receives consistent skill reinforcement.
Target the documented area of academic need while preserving strengths in unaffected subjects.
Interpret the persistent academic bottleneck as evidence of broadly limited cognitive ability across every learning domain.
Assign an instructional aide to complete the demanding academic steps so the young child can keep pace with class assignments.
items.rationale: Specific learning disabilities can affect particular psychological processes and academic skills unevenly. Instruction should be based on the young child’s actual pattern of strengths and needs, not a global assumption. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Applying blanket remediation across strong subjects wastes instructional time, lowers engagement, and ignores the defining uneven skill profile typical of specific learning disabilities.

Correct. Specific learning disabilities can affect particular psychological processes and academic skills unevenly. Instruction should be based on the young child’s actual pattern of strengths and needs, not a global assumption. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Specific learning disabilities affect targeted processing and academic skills rather than overall intellectual capacity, so inferring broad cognitive limits misinterprets the young child’s profile.
Having an adult complete the challenging task prevents skill acquisition, creates prompt dependence, and substitutes completion for specially designed instruction.

items.prompt: A young child with autism covers their ears during fire-drill announcements and then misses directions. Which support is most responsive?
choices: Treat covering the ears and missing directions as task refusal and apply standard classroom behavior consequences.
Excuse the young child from participating in future schoolwide drills or timed transitions to avoid triggering sensory distress.
Build a predictable warning and accessible cueing routine while teaching the young child how to use it.
Continue using loud, unannounced signals without preparation so the young child gradually desensitizes through repeated exposure.
items.rationale: Sensory and communication needs can affect access and behavior. A predictable warning, accessible direction, and taught coping or communication response support participation while preserving safety requirements. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Treating sensory overload as willful defiance misreads a neurobiological access barrier and can escalate distress without teaching an effective safety or transition response.
Excluding the young child from safety drills or transitions undermines safety preparedness and reduces inclusive participation when proactive sensory supports can enable success.

Correct. Sensory and communication needs can affect access and behavior. A predictable warning, accessible direction, and taught coping or communication response support participation while preserving safety requirements. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Unprepared exposure to painful or overwhelming auditory stimuli risks trauma and escalation rather than building self-regulation or reliable response to emergency directions.

items.prompt: A young child with ADHD begins work when directions are chunked and a checklist is visible. What does this pattern suggest?
choices: The young child already mastered the self-management skills needed and had been choosing not to start earlier assignments.
Adding checklists and interim milestones has lowered the rigor of the grade-level academic standard being assessed.
The young child’s uneven project completion reflects limited intellectual understanding of the content rather than self-regulation.
Executive-function scaffolds are strengthening task initiation, planning, and self-monitoring.
items.rationale: ADHD may affect executive functions such as initiation, working memory, inhibition, and organization. External structures can support performance without changing the learning target or implying weak ability. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Responding well to external structure is a hallmark of executive-function support needs, not evidence of intentional noncompliance or lack of motivation.
Chunking directions and setting interim checkpoints support organization and initiation while keeping the underlying academic content and rigor intact.
Completing the same content accurately once tasks are structured demonstrates intact conceptual capability paired with executive-function barriers to independent planning.

Correct. ADHD may affect executive functions such as initiation, working memory, inhibition, and organization. External structures can support performance without changing the learning target or implying weak ability. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.

items.prompt: A young child with an emotional or behavioral disability argues mainly during unpredictable peer-group tasks. What perspective is most useful?
choices: Analyze interactions among the young child, task structure, peers, expectations, and consequences.
Expect the same level of emotional conflict across every school setting because the disability resides within the young child.
Conclude that same-age peers’ interpersonal habits are the sole cause of the young child’s behavioral difficulties during group work.
Replace peer-group and cooperative learning tasks with independent seatwork for the remainder of the academic year.
items.rationale: An ecological perspective considers how behavior emerges through interactions between the young child and the environment. Context-specific data can guide prevention, instruction, and reinforcement of more effective responses. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Correct. An ecological perspective considers how behavior emerges through interactions between the young child and the environment. Context-specific data can guide prevention, instruction, and reinforcement of more effective responses. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Assuming behavior is invariant across contexts ignores the clear contextual contrast shown in the scenario and misses preventive instructional levers.
Blaming peers alone oversimplifies a reciprocal interaction and ignores how clear roles, expectations, and taught social skills can improve participation.
Eliminating collaborative opportunities permanently removes vital social-learning contexts and restricts access to inclusive peers instead of teaching structured participation.

items.prompt: Which information is essential when considering educational needs associated with intellectual disability?
choices: A standardized oral reading fluency and comprehension score collected during a single school screening window.
Combined evidence of cognitive functioning and adaptive behavior across conceptual, social, and practical domains.
Medical history records and physical growth measurements gathered from the young child’s primary health-care provider.
Anecdotal early childhood special educator ratings describing the young child’s adherence to rules inside one general education classroom.
items.rationale: Intellectual disability involves limitations in intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior. Educational planning therefore considers functional conceptual, social, and practical performance across relevant environments. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: A single academic reading measure cannot capture broader intellectual functioning or everyday social and practical adaptive skills needed to plan comprehensive supports.

Correct. Intellectual disability involves limitations in intellectual functioning and adaptive behavior. Educational planning therefore considers functional conceptual, social, and practical performance across relevant environments. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Medical history may inform health accommodations, but it does not document cognitive functioning or adaptive performance across school, home, and community settings.
Informal impressions from one classroom omit cross-setting adaptive evidence and standardized cognitive information required for accurate educational planning.

items.prompt: A young child understands grade-level ideas but has difficulty producing clear speech. What is the most appropriate instructional assumption?
choices: Simplify the cognitive complexity of class questions so the young child can participate with brief, low-demand responses.
Speak for the young child during whole-class discussions so the pacing of the lesson remains smooth for same-age peers.
Presume competence, support an accessible response mode, and separate spoken output from content mastery.
Require spoken oral answers during formal checks so the young child gets daily practice in expressive articulation.
items.rationale: A communication disability can limit how knowledge is expressed without indicating limited understanding. Accessible response modes and adequate wait time help the young child demonstrate the intended construct. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Lowering cognitive rigor confuses speech-production barriers with intellectual capacity and deprives the young child of grade-level conceptual challenge.
Answering on the young child’s behalf silences the young child’s voice, denies authentic communication practice, and prevents accurate assessment of what the young child knows.

Correct. A communication disability can limit how knowledge is expressed without indicating limited understanding. Accessible response modes and adequate wait time help the young child demonstrate the intended construct. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Insisting on spoken production when speech is the barrier measures speech motor skill instead of the intended academic construct and blocks equitable participation.

items.prompt: A young child has both a visual impairment and a motor disability. How should the team plan access?
choices: Attach standard classroom accommodations for each separate disability label without trialing how they work together.
Prioritize accommodations for the young child’s primary eligibility category while keeping other routines unchanged.
Predict all classroom barriers directly from diagnostic descriptions so lab trials are not necessary before starting.
Evaluate how the combined needs interact in each task and coordinate supports across specialists.
items.rationale: Co-occurring disabilities may interact in ways that are not captured by treating each label separately. Collaborative task analysis and trials show how combined access, communication, positioning, and health supports function. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Stacking isolated accommodations without testing them together can create conflicts—for instance, enlarging print in a way that exceeds a young child’s safe physical reach.
Addressing only one eligibility label leaves interacting sensory, motor, or health barriers unaddressed and risks unsafe or inaccessible participation.
Diagnostic categories describe broad patterns, not how a specific young child’s multiple needs interact with particular equipment, lighting, acoustics, and positioning.

Correct. Co-occurring disabilities may interact in ways that are not captured by treating each label separately. Collaborative task analysis and trials show how combined access, communication, positioning, and health supports function. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.

items.prompt: A young child with dyslexia reads familiar words from memory but struggles to decode new words. Which instruction most directly addresses the need?
choices: Explicit, systematic instruction in phonics, word analysis, and cumulative decoding practice.
Extended independent silent reading time with self-selected books and minimal adult interruption or feedback.
Repeated flashcard drills aimed at memorizing the visual outline of each new grade-level vocabulary word.
Replacing print reading instruction with audio recordings across all literacy and content-area assignments.
items.rationale: Dyslexia commonly involves accurate or fluent word recognition, decoding, and spelling. Explicit, systematic instruction with modeling, guided practice, cumulative review, and feedback directly addresses these skills. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Correct. Dyslexia commonly involves accurate or fluent word recognition, decoding, and spelling. Explicit, systematic instruction with modeling, guided practice, cumulative review, and feedback directly addresses these skills. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Unstructured silent reading without explicit decoding instruction and corrective feedback allows guessing habits to persist rather than building reliable word-reading skills.
Whole-word visual memorization breaks down as vocabulary expands and does not equip the young child to decode unfamiliar multisyllabic words independently.
While audio supports content access, replacing decoding instruction entirely denies the young child systematic intervention needed to build foundational literacy.

items.prompt: Two young children share the same disability category but respond differently to the same scaffold. What should the early childhood special educator do?
choices: Maintain uniform instructional scaffolds for both young children so accommodations match their shared eligibility category.
Use individual performance data to select, monitor, and adapt supports for each young child.
Keep the original scaffold unchanged for fairness until the end of the grading period before comparing outcomes.
Request a reevaluation immediately because divergent responses indicate that one young child was misclassified.
items.rationale: A disability category does not prescribe a single instructional profile. Individualized planning uses current performance, preferences, goals, and response data to decide which supports help each young child. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Standardizing supports by eligibility label ignores wide within-category variability and contradicts IDEA’s core requirement for individualized programming.

Correct. A disability category does not prescribe a single instructional profile. Individualized planning uses current performance, preferences, goals, and response data to decide which supports help each young child. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Fairness in special education means providing what each young child needs to access learning, not keeping an ineffective scaffold in place for uniformity.
Different responses to a single instructional tool reflect normal young child variability rather than diagnostic error and call for instructional adjustment, not automatic reclassification.

items.prompt: A young child with low vision receives a worksheet containing a dense unlabeled diagram. What is the best access response?
choices: Substitute an easier vocabulary activity from an earlier unit so the young child can work independently without visual media.
Provide a classmate’s completed responses so the young child can record the conclusions without interpreting the figure.
Provide an equivalent accessible format—such as a verbal description, tactile graphic, or usable enlargement.
Allow extended time on the original worksheet while keeping the dense visual graphic unchanged in size and contrast.
items.rationale: Access means preserving the intended concept while changing how information is perceived when necessary. The appropriate representation depends on the young child’s assessed media and access needs. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Substituting an unrelated lower-level task strips away access to the target concept instead of making the grade-level information perceptible.
Copying a peer’s answers removes conceptual engagement and assessment validity rather than enabling the young child to analyze the information directly.

Correct. Access means preserving the intended concept while changing how information is perceived when necessary. The appropriate representation depends on the young child’s assessed media and access needs. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
Extra time does not resolve a visual-access barrier if the underlying diagram or small graph remains unreadable or unperceivable to the young child.

items.prompt: A young child who is deaf uses sign language and will join a small-group story and discussion activity. Which plan best supports communication access?
choices: Assign front-row seating near the early childhood special educator’s desk as the primary accommodation for full seminar participation.
Replace live seminar discussions with written summaries so the young child can earn participation credit independently.
Maintain rapid open-floor discussions without turn-taking cues so the young child experiences realistic peer pacing.
Address preferred mode, direct interaction opportunities, acoustics, assistive technology, and speaker visibility.
items.rationale: Communication access is broader than hearing volume. Planning should address the young child’s language and mode, visibility or audibility of speakers, technology, peer access, and direct instruction needs. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.
choiceRationales: Front-row seating alone cannot provide access to rapid multi-speaker peer dialogue, sign-language interpretation, visual turn-taking, or assistive listening needs.
Replacing live peer discussion with solitary written work restricts inclusive interaction and denies authentic communication participation with same-age peers.
Unstructured overlapping speech makes speechreading, interpreting, and assistive listening far less effective; clear speaker identification supports equitable access.

Correct. Communication access is broader than hearing volume. Planning should address the young child’s language and mode, visibility or audibility of speakers, technology, peer access, and direct instruction needs. For 5692 preparation, apply the decision to developmentally appropriate, family-centered services from birth through age eight and distinguish IDEA Part C IFSP processes from Part B IEP processes when relevant.

items.prompt: A young child with a physical disability needs support positioning materials during science lab. What is the early childhood special educator’s best action?
choices: Collaborate with the child and specialists to arrange a safe, accessible workspace and active lab participation.
Assign the young child to record observations from the side of the room during laboratory investigations for safety.
Adjust the young child’s wheelchair seating and lab reach setup independently based on quick classroom judgment.
Ask a lab partner to make experimental decisions and manipulate every tool while the young child watches the steps.
